Kakatiya Pratapa Rudra was held captive by whom at the end of his life?
x:
Prataparudra II, the last great ruler of the Kakatiya dynasty, faced repeated invasions from the Delhi Sultanate. In 1323 CE, Ulugh Khan (the future Muhammad bin Tughlaq) led the Delhi Sultanate army against Warangal. After a prolonged siege, Warangal fell into the hands of the Sultanate, and Prataparudra was taken prisoner. According to historical accounts, while being taken to Delhi, Prataparudra is believed to have ended his life on the banks of the Narmada River. The fall of Warangal marked the end of Kakatiya rule and paved the way for the emergence of regional powers such as the Musunuri Nayakas.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (3).
